incidents.victim: Mexican government agencies and Brazilian financial firms
incidents.vector: Two Latin American crews jailbroke an AI agent (pretending it was an authorized red-team) and used it to scan, exploit, and pivot across victim networks, with the model generating bespoke backdoors and Python tools on the fly.
incidents.impact: Six Mexican federal entities were compromised between late December and early January, leading to data theft, and a separate Brazilian-Portuguese-speaking crew hit financial firms in Brazil to steal financial data; the dynamically generated tooling evaded signature-based detection.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an unspecified vulnerability in Skoda's German online store.
incidents.impact: Skoda confirmed customer data was likely accessed; scope and notification status are still under investigation.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an issue in Instructure's Free-For-Teacher accounts to access the Canvas platform on May 1, then re-entered on May 7 after Instructure said the incident was contained — defacing Canvas login pages with extortion demands for 330 institutions.
incidents.impact: Roughly 3.65 TB of data on 275 million students and staff (names, emails, student IDs, course messages) was claimed stolen; Canvas was taken offline during final exams; Instructure paid the ransom and the data was claimed deleted, House Homeland Security has launched an investigation, and the FBI is engaged.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached the corporate network on May 4, exfiltrated data, and encrypted systems; the entry vector has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: Global shipping, receiving, and manufacturing of injectable drug-delivery components were disrupted (West supplies stoppers, seals, and auto-injector components to major drug makers); core enterprise systems are restored but some sites are still being brought back online. Disclosed via SEC 8-K; Unit 42 leading the investigation.

incidents.vector: Ransomware deployment forced multiple North American sites offline beginning the weekend of May 8; entry vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Wisconsin and other US/Mexico factories saw network outages, and staff were sent home with operations forced to paper-and-pen; attackers claim 8 TB stolen including technical drawings tied to Apple, Google, and NVIDIA orders. Plants are resuming production.

incidents.vector: Hundreds of malicious Ruby packages were published over two days to deliver cross-site scripting payloads and steal data from RubyGems engineers and staff.
incidents.impact: RubyGems disabled new user sign-ups and is still triaging what attackers tried to exfiltrate; this is in addition to (and unrelated to) the simultaneous TanStack/npm worm.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion; attackers exfiltrated proprietary source code and demanded a ransom.
incidents.impact: After Vodafone refused to pay, the criminal group published source code from internal Vodafone systems.

incidents.vector: An undisclosed intrusion gave attackers access to Best Western's reservation systems for roughly six months (October 2025 through April 2026).
incidents.impact: Guest data from Best Western, Sure Hotels, and WorldHotels brand properties was exposed; the chain has begun guest notifications.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party IT services provider, then used the customer's HPE Operations Manager/Operations Agent monitoring platform to push malicious VBScripts to web servers and domain controllers; they registered a rogue network provider (mslogon.dll) and a password filter (passms.dll) on DCs to capture plaintext credentials.
incidents.impact: Stealthy, malware-light campaign maintained persistent credential theft and lateral movement for ~123 days before Microsoft Incident Response was engaged; intrusion is being held up by Microsoft as a model of trusted-relationship abuse that bypassed conventional detection.

incidents.victim: TanStack, UiPath, MistralAI and ~400 downstream npm packages
incidents.vector: Attackers triggered automated package publish workflows using an 'orphaned commit' to abuse over-broad GitHub Actions permissions, then shipped a 2.3 MB obfuscated payload that ran via the Bun JavaScript runtime, scraped AWS/GCP/Kubernetes/HashiCorp Vault credentials, embedded itself in .vscode/ and .claude/ config files, and exfiltrated stolen secrets over the Session messaging app.
incidents.impact: Credential-stealing malware was injected into packages with more than 12 million weekly downloads (TanStack's React Router alone); the worm spoofed Anthropic Claude bot commits to spread further and left ransom notes threatening to wipe systems if developers rotated tokens. Tagged the 'Mini Shai-Hulud' campaign.

incidents.victim: Russian aerospace firms and drone operators
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing and malvertising lured victims to download trojanized installers for aviation software, including a fake project on SourceForge; multi-stage, fileless JavaScript RATs and PowerShell tooling, plus a Windows shortcut exploit (ZDI-CAN-25373) used in other APT campaigns.
incidents.impact: Operators harvested GPS data, GIS shapefiles, digital relief files, and proprietary mapping files from Russian government and enterprise systems — data with direct value for logistics disruption, terrain mapping, and asset tracking. Tracked by Kaspersky, Positive Technologies, and BI.ZONE since at least September 2025.

incidents.victim: Users of a popular open-source web-based admin tool (intervention before launch)
incidents.vector: A prominent cybercrime group used a large language model to develop a Python-based zero-day exploit that bypasses two-factor authentication on a widely-used open-source administration tool; Google Threat Intelligence Group identified the code by its AI-style docstrings, a hallucinated CVSS score, and overly textbook structure.
incidents.impact: Google disclosed the bug responsibly and disrupted the planned mass-exploitation campaign before launch; Google describes this as the first documented criminal AI-developed zero-day and the 'tip of the iceberg.'

incidents.vector: Attackers maintained undetected access inside the water utility's network for nearly two years before the original intrusion was discovered — a delayed disclosure of the 2022 ransomware incident.
incidents.impact: UK Information Commissioner's Office fined South Staffordshire Water nearly £1 million for failing to detect the intruders; underscores ongoing concern about persistent access into UK critical-infrastructure operators.

incidents.victim: Huge Networks (Brazilian DDoS-protection ISP) and downstream Brazilian ISPs
incidents.vector: An exposed open directory revealed Portuguese-language Python tooling and SSH private keys for the CEO of Huge Networks; the attacker maintained root access to Huge Networks' infrastructure and used it to build a DNS-reflection/amplification botnet from misconfigured routers and DNS servers.
incidents.impact: The botnet powered an extended campaign of massive DDoS attacks against other Brazilian ISPs — the very customers Huge Networks was meant to protect. Huge Networks attributes the activity to a security breach by a competitor.

incidents.victim: CB Financial Services (Carmichaels, PA — state commercial bank)
incidents.vector: Not disclosed in the SEC filing.
incidents.impact: CB Financial Services filed an 8-K Item 1.05 Material Cybersecurity Incident notice with the SEC on May 11 (period of report May 7); detail beyond the filing is not yet public.

incidents.victim: US Department of Defense (service members and training records)
incidents.vector: Schemata, a DoD-contracted AI virtual training platform, left an API exposed online with no authentication.
incidents.impact: Service member records and sensitive military training documents were retrievable for an extended period; Schemata took roughly 150 days to secure the API after responsible disclosure.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained access to Braintrust's AWS infrastructure and may have reached the company's API key database.
incidents.impact: Braintrust instructed customers — including Cloudflare, Vercel, and Stripe — to rotate API keys; the company sells AI model monitoring used by major tech firms, raising downstream supply-chain concerns.

incidents.vector: Smart-contract or wallet-level exploit (specifics not yet disclosed).
incidents.impact: $1.4 million in crypto assets drained from the Ekubo Protocol.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM)
incidents.vector: Improper input validation vulnerability (CVE-2026-6973) in Ivanti EPMM under active exploitation.
incidents.impact: CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and required federal agencies to patch; multiple sectors have historically been targeted via Ivanti EPMM bugs.

incidents.victim: Selected government, scientific, manufacturing and retail organizations in Russia, Belarus, and Thailand
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised AVB Disc Soft's site and signed DAEMON Tools installers with a legitimate vendor certificate; the trojanized installers (in distribution since at least April 8) profiled hosts and delivered the QUIC RAT only to high-value targets.
incidents.impact: Several thousand hosts received the first-stage backdoor; a dozen carefully selected targets in Russia/Belarus/Thailand were given the second-stage RAT. Kaspersky links the operation to Chinese-speaking actors and notes the pattern mirrors prior trusted-software supply-chain operations.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; attackers gained access to industrial control systems at multiple sites.
incidents.impact: Poland's intelligence service (ABW) confirmed five water treatment facilities were compromised last year, with ICS access at some sites. No public attribution.

incidents.vector: Authentication bypass plus remote code execution in cPanel/WHM (CVE-2026-41940) affecting every version since 2013; patched April 30 and under active exploitation.
incidents.impact: Australia's ACSC issued a critical alert citing active exploitation in Australia and urged immediate patching across cPanel/WHM estates; given cPanel's ubiquity in shared hosting, exposure is broad.

incidents.vector: Unspecified intrusion into the national healthcare database; Moldova's Cybersecurity Agency did not rule out Russian involvement and said no ransom was demanded.
incidents.impact: Personal and financial information for nearly every adult in Moldova (citizens and insured foreigners) was exposed; about 30% of the agency's data was affected, with files either stolen or restored from backups. Comes as Russia escalates pressure on Moldova politically and militarily via Transnistria.

incidents.victim: Embassy of Cuba in Washington, D.C.
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a Microsoft Exchange email server at the Cuban embassy as part of a broader campaign that hit more than 5,000 Exchange servers worldwide this year.
incidents.impact: Chinese operators exfiltrated Cuban diplomats' mailboxes, reportedly to monitor and inform Beijing on the US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz region.
